scope_and_depth.budget_check: R850 specifies 1,500-2,000 substantive words and at most seven primary URLs; report is 1,813 whitespace-delimited words and cites one external primary URL.
scope_and_depth.judgment: Strong, bounded source/lifetime audit. It traces the actual callback, one-row head, readback, host reduction, and outer ownership transaction; it preserves the failure as unexplained and does not transfer the earlier separate-queue regression onto this path. It separates observed receipt facts from ranked hypotheses and offers progressively safer discriminators.
strengths: Correctly identifies that NLL wraps the prior callback and processes each chunk's dense rows before selected-logit/MTP callbacks; selected.bin remaining empty is expected for a stall in that loop.

Correctly follows the same explicit main queue through GR/native or canonical head work, D2H copy, and checked synchronization; the callback guard keeps borrowed rows and scratch alive through that drain.
Correctly separates GPU projection/readback from host FP64 reduction and file writing, and labels the 32,862-row all-position NLL path as a high-cost diagnostic rather than a performance sample.
Correctly treats the four-byte partial record, absent row timestamps, and nearby CCS reset as insufficient to locate or explain the stall.
limits: A successful single selected-logit row at position 677 would test one head/readback instance. It would not reproduce the dense callback loop, cumulative resource or state effects, CPU reducer, or repeated stdio path, so it cannot falsify the broader failure mechanism.

The proposed observer's phase list includes after-readback-submit and after-sync but omits before-sync, despite the discriminator relying on a before-sync/after-sync pair. A later after-sync marker only shows the wait returned before observation ended; it does not rule out a prior long interval or a different stall.

The parent-visible status record needs a coherent snapshot protocol (for example, a sequence counter or atomic phase plus validated fields) to avoid torn or stale cross-process reads. Wall-clock timestamps alone also do not separate host computation/submission from CPU consumed inside waits; record thread CPU deltas for submit, poll/wait, reduction, and append phases.
The CPU mock can check guard control-flow branches, but cannot establish device pointer validity, real SYCL event/queue behavior, or driver resource lifetime.

R850's Yama1 recommendation is directionally safe only when the tracer is an allowed ancestor/parent relationship and classic dumpability/credential checks pass. The actual tracer PID must be verified in the launch design; a sibling debugger is not made safe by being owned by the same user. The report should cite the official Yama rule.

primary_source_verification.status: R850's SYCL contract claims were checked against Khronos SYCL 2020 revision 12. Yama1 guidance was checked against Linux kernel documentation because the report uses it but does not cite it.

sources.title: Khronos SYCL 2020 Specification, revision 12
verified_claims: The queue in_order property orders commands submitted to that queue, without ordering commands from other queues.
queue::wait_and_throw waits for all previously submitted queue commands and delivers unconsumed asynchronous errors to the handler.

handler::memcpy explicitly permits each endpoint to be a host pointer or an accessible USM pointer. Thus std::vector-backed host storage is contractually permitted for this copy, subject to lifetime and extent; the spec does not establish Intel runtime staging, page-locking, lack of blocking, or performance behavior.

sources.title: Linux kernel Yama documentation
verified_claims: ptrace_scope=1 restricts PTRACE_ATTACH to the allowed parent/descendant relationship by default, subject to classic dumpability and credential checks; an inferior may explicitly authorize a debugger with PR_SET_PTRACER.

No sysctl change is needed for a correctly parented, otherwise permitted debugger. The proposed design must verify the actual tracer/inferior relationship and eligibility before relying on stack capture.

primary_source_verification.conclusion: No concrete callback source-level use-after-free, wrong same-queue dependency, out-of-bounds row, or direct prefill/session scratch alias was found. Pageable D2H behavior and runtime/driver progress remain unmeasured hypotheses, not contract defects or established causes.

claim_corrections.issue: The one-row selected-logit run is narrower than the failed dense NLL callback. A pass cannot clear repeated-loop, cumulative, reducer, or writer hypotheses.
claim_corrections.action: Label the outcome as a single-row head/readback discriminator. Keep it conditional on a new independent health gate and do not relabel or replace the incomplete exhaustive result.

claim_corrections.issue: The described phase list has no before-sync marker, while the proposed interpretation depends on one. It records wall time but no per-thread CPU time.
claim_corrections.action: Add paired before-sync/after-sync timestamps; measure thread CPU around host submission, wait/poll, target_loss, and append. Publish a bounded, coherent cross-process snapshot. Interpret after-sync only as proof that that wait returned before the observer's deadline.

claim_corrections.issue: R850 invokes Yama1 to justify the proposed parent-owned stack capture but its source list omits the Linux kernel policy documentation.
claim_corrections.action: Index this review's primary source check and state that the exact tracer relationship plus dumpability/credential eligibility must be verified before a future stack-capture proposal. Do not change ptrace policy.

claim_corrections.issue: The SYCL standard permits ordinary host pointers for handler::memcpy, but this does not prove absence of backend staging, hidden synchronization, or pageable-memory stalls on the installed Intel stack.
claim_corrections.action: Keep the ordinary pageable D2H path as an unresolved implementation/runtime hypothesis unless a safe phase observation attributes time to it.

claim_corrections.issue: The CPU mock proposed for DraftUploadGuard can exercise its injected drain/fatal branches but cannot qualify real device queue/resource behavior.
claim_corrections.action: Use it only to rule on guard control flow; retain runtime and device lifetime questions as open until supported by separately authorized, safely gated evidence.
